record.original_question: For every positive integer n divisible by 4, does there exist an n x n Hadamard matrix (a matrix with entries in {+1,-1} and mutually orthogonal columns)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 14 (Hadamard Conjecture). For any positive n a multiple of 4, there exists an n×n Hadamard matrix.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An $n \times n$ matrix $H$ with entries in $\{+1, -1\}$ is called a Hadamard matrix if its columns are pairwise orthogonal, equivalently if $H H^{\top} = n I_n$, where $I_n$ denotes the $n \times n$ identity matrix. It is known that if a Hadamard matrix of order $n > 2$ exists, then $n$ must be divisible by $4$.

Prove or disprove: for every positive integer $n$ that is a multiple of $4$, there exists an $n \times n$ Hadamard matrix.
artifact.status_search_result: The Hadamard conjecture remains a famous open problem in combinatorics. The smallest order for which existence is currently unknown is $n = 668$ (after the order $428$ case was resolved by Kharaghani and Tayfeh-Rezaie in 2004). No general construction is known.

status_evidence.title: Hadamard matrix - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Hadamard conjecture proposes that a Hadamard matrix of order 4k exists for every positive integer k. ... As of 2014, the smallest order for which no Hadamard matrix is known is 668.
status_evidence.claim: The Hadamard conjecture is still open; smallest unresolved order is 668.

status_evidence.title: A Hadamard matrix of order 428 (Kharaghani, Tayfeh-Rezaie)
status_evidence.snippet: We construct a Hadamard matrix of order 428, settling the smallest previously open case.
status_evidence.claim: Order 428 was resolved in 2005, but the conjecture as a whole remains open.
